A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VisionTS work. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial layout changes.

before.justification: v2 reports original VisionTS forecasting results, fine-tuning experiments, ablations, runtime measurements, and qualitative examples in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains original VisionTS experiments and additionally reports GIFT-Eval performance, a periodicity-selection control, and LaMa backbone results.

M1.justification: v3 adds LaMa as an alternative visual-inpainting backbone for VisionTS (Section 4.2, Table 14), extending the model family. The principal MAE pipeline, segmentation, normalization, alignment, reconstruction, and layer-normalization fine-tuning remain unchanged.

E1.justification: v3 adds GIFT-Eval, described as 23 datasets spanning seven domains, ten frequencies, and short-to-long forecasting horizons, while removing the separately reported six-dataset PF evaluation. Long-term TSF and Monash coverage remain. The PDFs do not enumerate all dataset overlap between GIFT-Eval and the retained or removed suites.

E2.justification: The new GIFT-Eval comparison includes Lag-Llama, Timer, TTMs, and Chronos variants alongside MOIRAI and TimesFM. The runtime comparison adds PatchTST and DeepAR. Removing the PF comparison also removes its TiDE, TFT, and other comparator entries; retained long-term and Monash comparator sets are unchanged.

E3.justification: v3 specifies a fixed context length of 2000 for GIFT-Eval and adds a P = 1 control, while removing the PF protocol reporting sMAPE, MASE, ND, and NRMSE. Retained experiment settings and training budgets match. The new benchmark metric is inconsistent: Appendix B.1 says MAPE, whereas Figure 4 and Section 4.1 say normalized MASE.

E4.justification: v3 adds a direct comparison of selected periodicity against P = 1 (Table 7) and tests transfer beyond MAE using LaMa (Table 14). Existing model-size, interpolation, orientation, hyperparameter, fine-tuning, and qualitative analyses are retained rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: Both versions report three repeated full-shot runs with identical standard-deviation entries, relocated from v2 Table 19 to v3 Table 18. Runtime measurements remain averages over 90 runs. No new uncertainty-reporting practice is introduced.

E6.justification: v3 newly reports first place on the plotted GIFT-Eval comparison, P = 1 average MSE of 0.559 versus 0.344 for selected periodicity, LaMa average MSE of 0.374, and additional runtime entries. The detailed PF results are removed. Matched long-term, Monash, full-shot, and existing ablation scores remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The forecasting definitions, normalization equation, and patch-alignment mathematics are equivalent in both versions. Neither version adds or removes substantive formal assumptions, theoretical results, or proofs.

C1.justification: v3 adds an introduction claim that its evaluation scale is the largest among existing TSF foundation models and updates the stated benchmark scope. The central contributions—image-based zero-shot forecasting and effective minimal fine-tuning—retain their meaning.

C2.justification: v3 interprets the LaMa results as evidence that transfer derives from image–time-series similarities rather than MAE alone. It expands the explanation of channel-independent forecasting and revises the limitations, dropping the explicit exogenous-covariate restriction and continual-pretraining discussion while retaining distribution-forecasting and multivariate-interaction limitations.

D1.justification: v3 discloses the GIFT-Eval context length and leaderboard location, while removing PF-specific periodicity selections and setup details. Existing code and library links, A800 hardware, optimizer, learning rate, batch size, and retained hyperparameter tables remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds references to GIFT-Eval (Aksu et al., 2024) and LaMa (Suvorov et al., 2022), and removes the PF metric references to Hyndman and Koehler (2006) and Yu et al. (2016). The central positioning against text-based and time-series-based foundation models remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 makes limited prose edits, expands and relocates the multivariate discussion, moves detailed text-based related work and the TimesFM/LLMTime comparison into appendices, folds limitations into the conclusion, and adds an impact statement. The main argument and section sequence remain largely intact.

P2.justification: v3 adopts a two-column main text and references, redraws Figure 2, adds GIFT-Eval and diagnostic displays, and removes the PF tables. Full-shot results move to the appendix behind a compact main-text count summary. Existing displays are extensively resized and relocated; the traditional-baseline table is duplicated as Tables 11 and 12.

improvement.justification: The new P = 1 control directly supports the periodicity-selection choice, and the LaMa experiment extends evidence beyond MAE. These provide useful additional validation while established results remain intact. The gains are tempered by removal of detailed PF results and incomplete GIFT-Eval reporting, including the MAPE/MASE inconsistency and absence of per-dataset results.
